subject.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path

question: Where should OpenClaw enforce owner-tier authority for Skill Workshop authoring, lifecycle mutation, and approval resolution?
rationale: The report is a concrete authorization bypass, but the durable security boundary spans command handling, agent tool/service execution, and approval resolution, so maintainers should choose the enforcement layer before automation changes the trust model.

options.title: Gate every mutation boundary
options.body: Require owner-tier authority before `/learn` starts authoring, before lifecycle apply/reject/quarantine execute, and before `/approve` resolves Skill Workshop plugin approvals.

options.title: Gate chat entry points only
options.body: Block non-owner `/learn` and `/approve` while leaving lower-level tool/service calls governed by existing approval policy, which is smaller but trusts callers more.

options.title: Fold into broader approval evidence design
options.body: Treat this as part of the wider lifecycle approval evidence work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93278, accepting that the concrete bypass remains open until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Gate every mutation boundary
recommendation.body: Require owner-tier authority before `/learn` starts authoring, before lifecycle apply/reject/quarantine execute, and before `/approve` resolves Skill Workshop plugin approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on same-chat approval routing and Skill Workshop lifecycle approval fixes, which are the central decision surfaces.
